signals: You sold within two weeks of reaching your target only 0 of 17 times.

name: Discounting news against your call

name: Buying at a bad time of day
Trading more than your information supports
signals: You turn over 178% of your depot a year; the average private investor in Barber & Odean's data turned over about 75%.

text: Do not place buys in the midday (11-15 h on your clock). Decide then if you like, and place the order at another time.
Do not buy while the market is as turbulent as on the most turbulent 33% of days (volatility above about 23% a year).
Do not buy right after one of the market's strongest stretches: its return over the last 20 days in the top 20% of days (above about 4.3%).
Do more research before you buy: look at the stock on at least about 1 occasion in the 30 days before (a conviction score of 1, the number on the watchlist's pills).
Do not buy a stock whose 12-month return is in the top 10% of the stocks you viewed in the last 30 days.
When you have looked at a stock on fewer than about 6 occasions in the last 30 days (a conviction score under 3), keep the buy to at most 1x your usual buy.
Do not buy a stock while other Stocktrails users look at it more than 3x as often as usual (the last 3 days against the month before). Wait until the crowd's attention fades.
